changelog.t: Nuzlocke fix: using an area (your first encounter there) could hide an item ball or make an old Emerald leader skip their TM, because the area records shared space with those items and TMs; picking up a Mega Stone could also mark an area as used. Areas now have their own space. An older Nuzlocke save is repaired once when you continue it: the areas you used carry over, and missing item balls, the old leaders' TMs and post-game eggs you never got come back.

Rustboro Mart sells its TMs (Round, Echoed Voice, Swagger, Pluck, Psych Up, Knock Off, Icy Wind, Draining Kiss) from the start. They used to wait for the Devon employee on Route 116, who only appears after the Slateport museum. Timer and Repeat Balls still come with him.

Rival Carlos: his second fight moved from Granite Cave to Slateport's road north to Route 110 (his team was above Gym 2's level cap, and most players do Granite Cave before the Gym). If you miss him on Jagged Pass he waits in Lavaridge, on the way to the Gym, and if you miss him in Victory Road he waits in Ever Grande City, before the League. Before, a missed fight was skipped.

Regular trainers have 5 Pokemon at most: the Pokemon Breeders Isaac and Lydia (Route 117) and Gabrielle (Mt. Pyre), with their rematches, Fisherman Ronald (Route 132) and Pokefan Colton (S.S. Tidal) each drop their lowest-level one. Bosses, rivals and Carlos keep 6.

Pokemon Breeders keep six Pokemon but sit well under the level cap: Isaac and Lydia (Route 117) 26 to 20 on Hard, Gabrielle (Mt. Pyre) 48 to 42, rematches 6 lower too (never below a Pokemon's evolution level), with moves they can know at those levels.

Levels on the way to Gym 4 (Hard; Normal 2 lower): the four trainers on Route 111 right outside Mauville 35 to 29 (they had the desert's levels, which you can only cross after Gym 4), Route 111 north of the desert 33 to 31, and the four Route 118 trainers you can walk to from Mauville 40 to 30 (the three across the river stay at 40). A few moves those Pokémon couldn't know yet at the new levels were swapped.
HM moves can be forgotten like any other move (when learning a new move or at the Move Deleter). Field moves still only need the HM in your bag and its badge, not the move.
Shops show the move after each TM number (TM101 Knock Off), and so does the Mauville Game Corner's prize list.

Move relearner (summary screen, START): level-up moves and the moves of TMs in your bag, as before. Egg moves now unlock after the Hall of Fame, and each tutor move once you've reached the town of the tutor who teaches it (Verdanturf, Slateport, Mauville, Fallarbor, Lavaridge, Fortree, Lilycove, Mossdeep, Sootopolis, Pacifidlog); the Battle Frontier tutors' moves once you've been to the Frontier. Before, every egg and tutor move was free from the start. SELECT switches between the lists.

New-game option BOSSES: FORWARD / REWIND. In Rewind the 13 bosses appear in reverse order: Alder leads Rustboro's gym, then Marshal, Caitlin, Shauntal, Grimsley (your parent in Petalburg), Marlon, Drayden & Iris (unchanged), Skyla; the Elite Four are Clay, Elesa, Burgh and Chili, and Lenora is the Champion. Each slot keeps its levels, badge, level cap, items and TM, with teams built for the new person (early ones use lower evolutions). Chosen at a new game and locked afterwards. Every Rewind boss has their own rematch teams (gym rematches, Elite Four rematch and the post-game challengers in the Champion's room) and speaks in character: Alder stepped down as Champion to meet new trainers at the first gym, Marshal followed him to Dewford, Chili's brothers left to see other regions while he climbed the League, Lenora kept the Cave of Origin's records before becoming Champion and leads the Sootopolis story scenes, and Grimsley is your parent. Gym trainers, gym guides, signs, Pokémon Center and town people talk about the new order. Gym trainers use Pokémon of their new leader's type (same levels and items), each boss's ace stands beside them in the gym, League rooms and Champion's room, and PokéNav calls, titles and check pages follow the new order (about 300 lines in all). Each Rewind boss also has their own mid-battle lines (hit by a super-effective move, sending out their ace, Mega Evolving), for the first battle and the rematches.
The Exp. Share is in your Key Items from the start of a new game, already switched on (it used to come from Mom with the Running Shoes). Use it from the bag to switch it off.

Post-game rematches with the original Emerald leaders: after the Hall of Fame they offer a double battle (on every difficulty and battle mode) whenever you talk to them. The first win gives a shiny egg of their ace's family with its Hidden Ability: Nosepass, Timburr, Pichu, Numel, Munchlax, Swablu, Solrock and Lunatone, Skrelp. Debug menu: Gen5 guest trainers warps to each Kanto Elite Four member.

Sootopolis: Reshiram, Zekrom and Kyurem use uncompressed overworld sprites, so the legendaries scene no longer runs out of sprite memory (Reshiram and Zekrom were drawn from other sprites' graphics). No wild Pokémon appear on the water there during the crisis.

The Kanto Elite Four visit Hoenn after the Hall of Fame as optional battles: Lorelei (Slateport City), Bruno (Fallarbor Town), Agatha (Mt. Pyre exterior) and Lance (Ever Grande City). Each has a Mega and a legendary that cannot be caught (Articuno, Galarian Zapdos, Pecharunt, Roaring Moon), with the ace 2 levels under the Unova Elite Four rematch ace, and Normal easier than Hard. Winning gives a shiny egg with egg moves and its Hidden Ability: Axew, Deino, Dreepy or Dratini. In Doubles mode they fight double battles.

19 new TMs, TM101-TM119, placed along the story: Knock Off, Icy Wind and Draining Kiss in Rustboro (after the Devon employee), Sucker Punch on Route 115, Hyper Voice in Fallarbor, Iron Head in Meteor Falls, Power Gem on the Fiery Path, Earth Power in the Route 111 desert, Close Combat, Play Rough and Aura Sphere in Lavaridge, Dark Pulse and Moonblast at the Lilycove Department Store, Stealth Rock in Sootopolis; Toxic moves from the Fiery Path to the Fallarbor Mart. Nothing above power 70 is sold before Gym 2. Spikes, Heat Wave, Brave Bird, Dazzling Gleam and Dragon Pulse are rewards from the original Emerald gym leaders, who also give TMs that used to lie on the ground (Focus Punch, Iron Tail) or were sold (Facade).

The original Emerald gym leaders are back as optional battles. Roxanne, Brawly, Wattson, Flannery, Norman, Winona, Tate & Liza and Juan stand next to their old gym with their ace Pokémon and battle you whenever you ask. They tell you their top level first, and each one's ace is 2 levels under the ace of the leader who runs the gym now. Beating one gives a TM: Spikes, Focus Punch, Iron Tail, Heat Wave, Facade, Brave Bird, Dazzling Gleam, Dragon Pulse. In Doubles mode they all fight double battles. Toxic and Sandstorm are now sold in Fallarbor; Facade is no longer sold in Lilycove.

Normal mode, from Gym 6 on (story and post-game): boss teams keep their Pokémon, levels and Megas but are less of a wall. Each Pokémon has at most one move outside its own types (the ace two; post-game two and three), a team has at most 2 setup users, 2 Pokémon with a status move and 2 hidden abilities, and before the Elite Four at most 3 strong held items (Life Orb, Choice items, Focus Sash...). The dropped moves became strategy moves such as U-turn, Substitute, screens, recovery or hazards. Easy and Normal Doubles follow; Hard is unchanged. Debug menu: 'Gen5 Sootopolis scene' replays the legendaries in Sootopolis.

Start a new save for 2.8. The Items pocket holds 100 different items (it was 30) and the TM case 140, ready for the new TMs. A 2.7 save still loads and keeps its items, but later 2.8 changes are only guaranteed on a new save.

Fix: the Steven team-up in the Mossdeep Space Center always used the first three Pokémon in the party, whichever three you picked, when the game had just been loaded. The chosen three now fight. The Mirage Tower on Route 111 (Cover and Plume Fossils) can no longer be missed: it was a coin flip per visit, and after two visits without it, it stays visible until you go in. The credits summary now tells a Nuzlocke player that the rules end at the Hall of Fame. Hard: Lenora now has 4 Pokémon and Chili 5 (Numel is gone), with level-up moves only and no Eviolite, so the first two gyms are hard but fair under hardcore Nuzlocke rules. Hard Burgh and Elesa were re-tuned the same way: only moves you can have by then (level-up plus TMs sold or given up to that point), at most one coverage move each, at most two Pokémon with a paralysis/sleep/poison move, and each uses the TM their gym gives out (Struggle Bug, Volt Switch). Drayano's Gen VI changes are in: the 23 Gen VI Pokémon get his level-up moves (STAB and coverage arrive earlier) and Skrelp, Clauncher and Noibat evolve at 35, 33 and 44; Phantump evolves at Lv 23 or by friendship. In his spirit, slow Gen VII-IX lines evolve sooner (Dreepy 34, Drakloak 50, Sandygast 36, Hattrem and Morgrem 37, Silicobra 33, Corvisquire 34, Varoom 36) and some signature moves arrive earlier. Cynthia's Garchomp is now Mega Garchomp Z, and all 24 Champion's Room challengers are equally likely. Hard: Steven's team-up partners in the Mossdeep Space Center are now Metagross, Excadrill and Aggron at Lv 56-57, built like a Hard boss. Every Mega Evolution is again exactly 100 base stat total above its base form: 26 Mega forms (Venusaur, Beedrill, Raichu, Steelix, Ampharos, Mawile, Medicham, Camerupt, Altaria, Banette, Absol, Glalie, Froslass, Lopunny, Golurk, Malamar, Crabominable, Drampa, Falinks, Scovillain, Tatsugiri) received the same stat buffs as their base form in 2.5. Post-game level caps: once you have cleared the game the cap is the top level of the Elite Four rematch teams (Normal 76, Hard 78), and once the first rematch fight starts it becomes the Champion title defence level (Normal 80, Hard 82); before, the cap simply switched off. Documentation: every Mega form is now listed in the Pokémon Changes tab and the Dex Table, right under its base form, with its stats, change from the standard game, stone, where the stone is, and what it gains over the base form. Documentation fix: the Pokémon Changes tab compared the game with itself, so every +/- showed 0; it now compares with pokeemerald-expansion 1.17.1 (the other tabs that show what changed from the base game were blank for the same reason and are filled in too). Hard Doubles (Doubles mode on Hard) had been missed by the Hard retune: its early boss teams were still 6 Pokémon from the first gym with the old coverage-heavy sets. They are rebuilt from the retuned Hard teams (same sizes, same move rules), keeping the doubles pass (Protect, a spread attack, a support move) but only with moves the player can have by then; Lenora and Chili are no longer Hard-doubles walls (a simulation of the first two gyms as 2-v-2 fights went from 74% / 57% cleared to 100% / 69%, the same as Hard singles). Hard rivals (Cheren, Bianca, Montana) now grow one Pokémon past their Normal team instead of jumping to 6, and their early teams use the same move rules. Doubles mode, Normal and Hard: Protect (and Detect, King's Shield and the like) was on most Pokémon of every boss team; it is now rare. At most 1 Pokémon per team has it (2 on a 6-Pokémon team, and only for a clearly defensive build), many teams have none, only defensive or stall builds (tanks, Leftovers, Toxic, Recover) get it, and until the Lilycove Department Store sells the TM (Winona and earlier) only Pokémon that learn it by level-up can have it. 259 boss and rematch teams were changed; the Pokémon that lost it got an attack. Documentation: the Evolutions tab shows each Pokémon's alternative evolution methods on one line joined by OR (Karrablast, Shelmet, Phantump), spells out “while Shelmet is in the party” instead of a code name, and has a Basculin (White-Striped) row explaining how to get Basculegion.

Mauville Game Corner: coins cost a quarter as much (50 for ₽250). Pokémon prizes replace the dolls, in three tiers by badges (2 / 5 / 7), one of each; the last tier is the four Ultra Beasts. On a Nuzlocke a prize Pokémon is your Mauville City encounter (a new 65th area). New coin prizes: Wide Lens, Zoom Lens, Muscle Band, Wise Glasses, Ability Patch. Lilycove 5F: restoratives (Max Revive, Ethers, Elixirs, PP Up) and utility items (Everstone, Luxury and Premier Balls) replace the cushion and poster clerks.

Poké Marts sell berries so nobody has to farm: Oran, Cheri, Chesto, Pecha, Rawst, Aspear and Persim in every mart from Oldale on; Sitrus, Lum, Leppa, Figy, Wiki, Mago, Aguav and Iapapa in Fallarbor, Lavaridge, Fortree, Mossdeep, Sootopolis and the League mart (the resist berries were already in Lilycove 3F). Documentation fix: the fossil list now matches the game (Aerodactyl from Old Amber, Amaura from the Sail Fossil, Arctozolt from the Frost Fossil; it wrongly listed Dracozolt, Dracovish and Arctovish).

Nuzlocke and the legendaries. The Sealed Chamber now needs any Ghost-type Pokémon first and any Water type last (was Jellicent first), so losing a Jellicent can't lock out the Iron Crown, Boulder and Leaves. In any Nuzlocke mode: roaming legendaries (Tornadus, Thundurus) ignore the catch rules, and a roamer that is knocked out keeps roaming at full health (only a catch ends it); any other wild legendary, mythical, Ultra Beast or paradox Pokémon you knock out is not lost, it stays where it stood so you can fight and catch it again.

Fix: the Sealed Chamber (opens the Iron Boulder, Iron Leaves and Iron Crown chambers) needed Jellicent first and exactly Tirtouga last. Tirtouga evolves at 37, before Frillish reaches Jellicent at 40, and the fossil is a choice, so many players could not open it. Now any Water-type Pokémon in the last slot works (at least two Pokémon in the party). The braille reads "A WATER TYPE". Field-move puzzles (Rock Smash, Flash) and the Island Cave step puzzle were checked and are unchanged.

Fix: 20 gym trainers were invisible (Mossdeep Gym's Cooltrainers, Lavaridge Gym basement's Workers, Sootopolis Gym basement's Swimmers). Their sprites came from FireRed/LeafGreen and were only included in FRLG builds; the four sprites and two palettes are now in the normal build.

Rival Carlos' team shows a clearer evolution path across his five fights: Lotad, Lombre, Ludicolo; Litwick, Lampent (now from fight 3, since it evolves at 27), Chandelure; Applin to Appletun; Trubbish to Garbodor; Ferrothorn. Mega Hawlucha joins the team; Chandelure stays his partner and ace (it no longer Mega Evolves). Galvantula, Orbeetle and Dottler are gone from his teams. Easy, Normal, Hard, the doubles teams and the museum rematch all follow.

The three fishing rods are given by the gym leaders: Old Rod after gym 2, Good Rod after gym 4, Super Rod after gym 6 (the old NPCs still work and never double up). New games start with 30 Poke Balls. N's Ultra Beast scenes (Blacephalon at Mt. Chimney, Celesteela at the Space Center) now show the Pokémon on screen, and the debug menu has 'Gen5 UB scenes…' to warp to and replay them. Saves from earlier versions are not supported with this version's new wild tables.

Bosses and other trainers that used battle items in vanilla Emerald (Potions, Full Restores) carry them again on Normal and Hard: the Elite Four 2 Full Restores each, Alder 4, gym leaders and rivals their Potions. They had been dropped in the team rebalances. Easy still has none.

Pseudo-legendary lines (Dratini, Beldum, Deino, Dreepy, Duraludon) are easier to find in the mid and late game wild tables: 10–15% slots in Routes 115, 119, 120, 123, Meteor Falls, Seafloor Cavern, Routes 132 and 134 (fishing) and Victory Road, always in a middle stage. A typical run now meets about 1–2.

Level caps now follow the difficulty: Easy and Normal use the old caps; Hard's caps are 2 higher (matching Hard's trainers), so no gym leader, Elite Four member or Alder has a Pokémon above the level cap on any difficulty. Hard teams are unchanged.

Fix: the first battle (Birch's rescue on Route 101) used Patrat, which isn't in the Pokédex any more, so the foe showed as '??????????' and the debug ROM stopped on a blue 'disabled species' screen. It is a Lv 2 Lillipup now.

Every TM is in the game: 42 Gen V TMs (TM59–TM100) are sold in the shops along the story, and TM21 Frustration and TM49 Snatch are back. The TM case now holds 120 (it was 64); older saves are copied across on load.
Larvesta evolves into Volcarona at Lv 45 (was 59).
Documentation: each Pokédex card also lists egg moves and tutor moves (taught from the Relearn option on the summary screen's Moves page).
Hisuian Samurott and Hisuian Braviary can now be reached: Dewott (Lv 36) and Rufflet (Lv 40) evolve into the normal form by day and the Hisuian form at night, like Koffing, Petilil and Bergmite.
Hydrapple can now be reached: Dipplin learns Dragon Cheer at Lv 40, and Hydrapple needs a level-up while knowing it.

Documentation: the Pokédex tab is one card per Pokémon (stats with bars, abilities, evolution, where to find it, every level-up move and every TM/HM you can get in this game); the old table is tab 7b. Evolution text now shows the real conditions (friendship, time of day, recoil damage, Dragon Cheer).

Doubles mode: a new BATTLES option (SINGLE / DOUBLE) on the mode screen and at the League Clerk. DOUBLE turns every trainer battle where the trainer has 2+ Pokémon into a double battle (a 1-Pokémon trainer stays single; with only one Pokémon able to battle you get a single battle). Wild battles stay single.

Doubles mode on Normal and Hard: 60 bosses (gym leaders, rivals, Elite Four, N and the admins, Montana, Winston, Wally, Matt...) have their own doubles team: same Pokémon, levels and items, with Protect, spread moves and a support move. Easy keeps its singles teams.
No EVs: no Pokémon gains EVs, stats ignore EVs (trainer and Frontier teams included), the summary has no EV page, and trainers have no EV spreads. Every Pokémon still has 31 IVs.

No EV items: vitamins, Power items, Macho Brace, Wings and the EV-lowering berries are gone from shops, gifts, prize lists and berry trees (replaced by Rare Candies, PP Ups, Lum/Sitrus/Leppa trees and the like).
No affection effects for your Pokémon (no 'toughed it out', status shake-off, dodges, extra crits or EXP). N's scripted bond at the Mt. Pyre summit stays.

Shops: Slateport Mart sells the common evolution items; Slateport market's Energy Guru sells every type-boosting item, Eviolite, Light Clay, Black Sludge and the weather rocks; Lilycove 3F sells the consumable battle items (Focus Sash, Red Card, Eject Button, Air Balloon, Weakness Policy...); Mossdeep Mart sells Choice Band/Specs/Scarf, Life Orb and Assault Vest. Prices 3,000–10,000. Lilycove 2F still has every evolution item.

Ten new item balls: Eviolite, Rocky Helmet, Muscle Band, Leftovers, Expert Belt, Loaded Dice, Heavy-Duty Boots, Clear Amulet, Covert Cloak, Booster Energy. Battle Frontier vitamin clerk: battle items for 16 BP.
Fair items: no trainer, on any difficulty, holds an item the player couldn't have by then (78 items swapped; Mega Stones excepted).
Route 121: Breeders Myles and Pat have 3 Pokémon each (they team up into one double battle).

Fix: the Mega Evolution icon could show the wrong colours (Mega Scrafty vs the Devon Scope Zorua): the battle ran out of sprite palettes. Fix: the debug ROM's blue 'could not load palette for overworld encounter' screen on busy routes.
Fix: status moves showed a garbled category icon in the BW summary's Battle Moves page.
Every gym leader, Elite Four member and the Champion has their ace standing beside them; talk to it to hear its cry.
Snivy (Petalburg Woods) and Oshawott (Route 104) are wild during the story.
Trainers use far more Pokémon from the new Pokédex (about two thirds of all trainer Pokémon). Gym leaders keep their aces and their rematch Megas.
Every non-legendary Mega Stone for a Pokédex Pokémon is in the story (36 new item balls); the strong ones only from Route 119 on.

Hard mode rebalanced: gym leaders have no legendaries until their 3rd rematch, and their extra Pokémon are of the gym's type and no stronger than their best Normal Pokémon. (The team builder didn't recognise the expansion's legendary flags, which is how Bloodmoon Ursaluna, Reshiram and Zekrom got onto early gyms.)

Hard: the Elite Four and Alder keep their legendary in their rematches; gym leaders' 3rd and 4th rematches have one legendary of their type; every Champion's Room challenger except Prof. Birch brings one legendary, Paradox or Ultra Beast (Cresselia, Heatran, Mewtwo, Zacian, Shaymin and Naganadel are trainer-only).
Ordinary trainers no longer have legendaries (some route and gym trainers had Kyurem, Regidrago, Iron Leaves or Iron Crown); Drayden & Iris's 2nd rematch has no box legendaries.
Wally has one Hatterene and an Altaria. Preschooler Lily is now Sofie.
Hard route trainers keep their Pokémon and levels but play them better: best level-up moves for the level, best ability, a fitting nature and a held berry (no TMs or EVs).
No boss, on any difficulty, has more Pokémon than the player could have caught by then (Nuzlocke-style: one per reachable area with wild Pokémon, plus the starter and gifts).
New 'Pokémon Changes' tab: every stat, type, ability, learnset and move change from the standard games.
Caitlin's ace is Starmie, and it Mega Evolves.

One Mega on every late boss team: gyms 5–8 and their rematches (Clay: Excadrill, Skyla: Altaria, Drayden & Iris: Drampa, then Dragonite in the rematches, Marlon: Golisopod), the Elite Four (Grimsley: Scrafty, Shauntal: Chandelure, Caitlin: Starmie, Marshal: Falinks, which replaces Sirfetch'd), Alder (Dragonite), the Elite Four rematches, Steven, Wally's Champion-room team and every Champion's Room challenger (Prof. Birch: Venusaur, Cynthia: Garchomp, Red: Charizard X, N: Chandelure, Cheren: Lopunny, Colress: Eelektross, Bianca: Audino, Lily: Lopunny, Montana: Excadrill).
Rival Carlos uses Hawlucha instead of Orbeetle.

N's story teams use only Pokémon from the routes between his fights, plus Zoroark and Blacephalon at the end (Hawlucha at Mt. Chimney, Ferrothorn in the Plasma Hideout). His finale team includes Blacephalon.
Mid-battle lines updated for the 2.5 teams (Chili, Skyla, Caitlin, Colress, N, Zinzolin, Ghetsis, Giallo, Wally).
New Pokédex: 347 species (Carlos's list plus Tadbulb and Bellibolt), in story order. A new game is needed.
Gen I–V Pokémon use Redux 1.4.1 (Complete): stats, types, abilities, level-up moves, TM moves, evolutions and move changes.

Gen VI–IX Pokémon get a Redux-style rebalance: starters to 535 (Maushold Normal/Fighting, Dachsbun Fairy/Fire, Bellibolt Electric/Water, Lv 25), small buffs for single-stage Pokémon, extra moves for weak learnsets, Wimpod/Golisopod keep Wimp Out/Emergency Exit as the common ability.
Starters: Tandemaus, Fidough, Tadbulb; the rival takes the next one along. Post-game, Prof. Birch gives Snivy, Charcadet or Oshawott.
Every wild table rebuilt from the new Pokédex (at least two species each, at least two counters before each gym); new mass outbreaks.
Legendaries: Iron Crown (Colress's ace), Iron Boulder and Iron Leaves in the old chambers; Ultra Beasts after the wormholes; Genesect with Ghetsis; mythicals as free catches; Magearna from Mr. Stone.
Story Pokémon from the new Pokédex: Lotad in the intro, Wally's Hatenna, Steven's Beldum, new fossils, NPC Pokémon and trades.

Every trainer, the Type Specialists, Battle Frontier sets, contests and the randomizer use the new Pokédex; Easy and Hard rebuilt. Hard legendaries: Tornadus, Regidrago, Volcanion, Darkrai, Marshadow, Meloetta, Keldeo, Victini.
One mode screen at a new game and at the League Clerk: Difficulty, Level caps, Nuzlocke, Randomizer and Wild Pokémon on one page, each choice explained before you pick.
Hard: everything before Lenora plays like Normal (Montana's first fight and the Route 103 rival too); Lenora's gym trainers are +1 level; Hard proper and the SET battle style start with Lenora.

Post-game rematches are double battles: gym leaders, the Elite Four rematch, every Champion's Room challenger, Steven and Wally. Every rematch team has doubles moves (Protect, spread moves, one support move).
Steven's ace is Mega Metagross (trainer-only, like Cynthia's Garchomp).
Mid-battle lines for every boss (the trainer slides in): when their ace comes out, before a Mega Evolution, at your first super-effective hit (early bosses), and when a legendary is knocked out.

Truth or ideals: six story questions from N and Ghetsis; after the Hall of Fame, one of them (or both, in a double battle) waits at the Mt. Pyre summit. N's Pokémon share the bond your Pokémon get at max friendship; Ghetsis brings a storm.

Black 2/White 2 location pop-ups; an Instant text speed (default for new games); ORAS Dowsing Machine (the rival's Route 110 gift); daily random weather on most routes; roamer cue for Tornadus/Thundurus; EXP for catching.
Area previews when you walk into Petalburg Woods and the caves; a run summary at the Hall of Fame (play time, battles, catches, modes, True Nuzlocke losses).

Fixes: TM case fits every TM and HM (TM21 Frustration and TM49 Snatch retired; the S.S. Tidal man gives a Lucky Egg), Nuzlocke item notes and party gap, Easy teams' levels and moves, 7-letter names in text, name boxes, the black bar in battle text, shinies stay on the map, Vs. Seeker for older saves past badge 5.

Bianca's and Cheren's battle pictures had Ruby/Sapphire May's and Brendan's colours (Beta 1.5 bug). Red and Ace Trainer Carlos were invisible in the Champion's Room. Both fixed on Beta 1.5 and merged in.

New game asks: difficulty (Easy / Normal / Hard), Nuzlocke (off / True / Partial) and randomizer (off / Balanced / True), then level caps. The League Clerk changes the difficulty, ends a Nuzlocke run and shows the randomizer seed.
Hard: Lenora has 4 Pokémon, Chili 5, later gym leaders 6; rivals grow one Pokémon past Normal up to 6, legendaries on gyms 6–8, the Elite Four and Alder, fully trained teams and smarter AI.
18 Type Specialists across Hoenn, one per type, Lv 70 (67 Easy, 72 Hard), there from a new game. Each warns before battling and gives a held item; all 18 earn a Master Ball and the Catching Charm.

Rematches use the Vs. Seeker (from Dad with the fifth badge): works indoors, half the beaten trainers in view answer, gym leaders answer after the Hall of Fame. Each leader's first rematch gives a held item.

Newer items placed: Quick, Dusk and Johto balls in Poké Marts, 39 power/competitive items as item balls, resist berries in Lilycove, pinch berries held by wild Pokémon, legendary form items (DNA Splicers, Reveal Glass, Rusted Sword/Shield, Reins of Unity) once you catch the legendary, Genesect's Drives from Colress, Falinksite in the Safari Zone.

Same Emerald story beats, retold: Team Plasma (N, truth; old Team Magma role) and Neo Plasma (Ghetsis, ideals; old Team Aqua role) split in a civil war. Reshiram and Zekrom replace Groudon and Kyogre; Kyurem replaces Rayquaza.

Gym Leaders: Lenora (Rustboro, Normal), Chili (Dewford, Fire), Burgh (Mauville, Bug), Elesa (Lavaridge, Electric), Clay (Petalburg, Ground; your dad), Skyla (Fortree, Flying), Drayden & Iris (Mossdeep, Dragon, double), Marlon (Sootopolis, Water).
Elite Four: Grimsley, Shauntal, Caitlin, Marshal. Champion: Alder. Rivals: Cheren or Bianca, and Carlos (five story fights). Elite Trainer Montana: five required fights before the League.
After your first Hall of Fame the Champion's Room holds a random challenger instead of Alder (24 possible).
Rebuilt teams with items, natures and smarter AI (no EVs since 2.6); optional hard level caps at the next leader's ace.
Wild Pokémon have a 10% chance of their hidden ability. Steven gives the Mega Ring and Audinite in Granite Cave.
Hoenn's towns and routes use LeoB's ORAS-style tilesets. Map layouts are unchanged.
Modern battle mechanics (pokeemerald-expansion 1.17.1), Gen 6+ Exp. Share and Gen 7 scaled EXP.

features.t: Running indoors, auto-run (L), Fast Surf (hold B), faster text (INSTANT in Options), B jumps to Run in wild battles.
HM-free field moves: once you own the HM and its badge, any party Pokémon can Cut / Rock Smash / Strength / Surf / Dive / Waterfall; Fly and Flash in every party menu. Fly from the Town Map (R).
Move relearner on the summary screen (START on the moves page), IV viewer (A on the skills page), nicknames from the summary.
Infinite Candy (key item, from the start; respects level caps) and Follow Bell (switches the following Pokémon).
Repel prompt when one runs out; last-used Ball (R) and move info (L) in battle; type icons in battle.
DexNav in the start menu (R searches for the registered species); visible wild Pokémon on by default (max 3 at a time), alongside normal random encounters.
Following Pokémon (lead Pokémon). Mass outbreaks reported on TV from the first badge.
Day/night tint. Deerling and Sawsbuck change form with the month's season.
League Clerk (scientist) in every Pokémon Center: switch level caps and visible wild Pokémon on or off; change the difficulty, end a Nuzlocke run, see the randomizer seed.

Difficulty: Easy (lower levels, basic AI), Normal, Hard (bigger boss teams: Lenora 4, Chili 5, then 6; rivals grow one past Normal; legendaries late, smart AI, SET style). Nuzlocke True (fainted Pokémon released) or Partial (catch rules only), 65 areas (Mauville City counts the Game Corner prize), dupes and shiny clauses. Randomizer Balanced (same stage, similar strength) or True (anything, legendaries included).

Shiny odds 1/4096; Shiny Charm (for completing the Pokédex) raises them to about 1/1365.

evos.now: Same as the official games, listed because it is easy to miss. Only the White-Striped form evolves (red- and blue-striped Basculin never do). It is a rare Super Rod catch (4%, Lv. 44-47) in 27 fishing areas, e.g. Route 102, Petalburg City, Route 107 (see the Encounters tab). Teach it a recoil move (Head Smash, Wave Crash, Double-Edge, Brave Bird...), take 294 HP of recoil in total across battles, then level up. Male Basculin become Male-form Basculegion, female ones the Female form.
